alphaandbetausers.title: Looking for early testers with multiple AI subscriptions: Sirus brings them into one terminal
alphaandbetausers.body:
I'm the maker of Sirus, an MIT-licensed terminal app for using existing Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions in one place, including multiple accounts from the same provider.

I'm looking for developers who already have that setup and can try one small task. The first thing I want to test is whether connecting your accounts and switching models feels straightforward. Agent teams and persistent project memory are there too, but account unification is the starting point.

What to try:
1. Install with npm install -g sirus-harness (Node.js 18+; Git for checkpoints).
2. Open a familiar project with sirus /path/to/project.
3. Run /login for each account, choose a model with /model, and try a small code question or change.

What would help me most: the step where you got stuck, whether you could use the accounts you intended, and what sent you back to another tool. You can reply here; no survey or meeting required. Please leave credentials and private code out of feedback.

Sirus itself is free and needs no separate account. Provider charges and limits still apply; this doesn't combine your quotas.

Install and examples: https://trysirus.com/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=first10&utm_content=beta

Anyone already juggling multiple subscriptions interested in trying their setup?

AI_Agents.body:
Sirus: your existing AI subscriptions, one terminal.

I'm the maker. Connect Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions, including multiple accounts from the same provider, then choose a model for each participant in a shared conversation. You can also delegate tasks to subagents and keep project memory between sessions.

For agent builders, the idea is to start with the accounts you already pay for and assemble a team around a real task. One participant implementing and another reviewing is one example; switching models yourself is useful too.

It's MIT-licensed, with no separate Sirus account. Provider charges and usage limits still apply; quotas aren't pooled.

Install: npm install -g sirus-harness
Start: sirus /path/to/project
Connect accounts with /login, then select with /model.

Examples and setup: https://trysirus.com/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=first10&utm_content=ai_agents

If you already run agents across different accounts, what's the most annoying part of keeping that setup together? I'd love feedback from a first task.

indiehackers.title: I built Sirus to bring existing AI subscriptions into one terminal — looking for first-use feedback
indiehackers.body:
I'm the maker of Sirus. The starting point is simple: if you already pay for Claude and ChatGPT, or have several accounts with one provider, you should be able to use them in one workspace.

Sirus is an open-source terminal app that connects those subscriptions. You can switch models, give participants different models in a shared conversation, and keep project memory for later sessions. It's free under MIT and doesn't require a separate Sirus account. Your provider bills and limits remain separate.

I'd like feedback on the first-use experience from other builders:
- Is connecting the accounts you already have enough of a reason to try a new terminal app?
- If you try it, where does the setup or model switching lose you?

Install: npm install -g sirus-harness
Open a project: sirus /path/to/project
Then /login for each account and /model to choose a starting model.

Setup and examples: https://trysirus.com/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=first10&utm_content=indiehackers

I'm recruiting the first people to try a real task, so candid feedback about what's missing is more useful to me than a star. Happy to answer setup questions here.
